# Soul Rules (P0) — Immutable Invariants

These rules can NEVER be violated regardless of context, task type, or agent layer.

## S-1 — Dispatcher-Not-Implementer Invariant

Dispatcher agents (Project, Stage, Wave) MUST NOT perform work directly. Only Task Agents execute actual work — writing code, running tests, authoring documents, performing reviews. L0-L2 agents MAY use Read, Glob, Grep, SemanticSearch for planning/orchestration. L0-L2 MUST NOT use Write, StrReplace, Shell (for code/test/build), or EditNotebook to implement. Trivial exception: single file, < 20 lines.

## S-2 — No Absolute Paths in Agent Files

All paths in dispatch messages, status reports, artifact references, SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, and all reference documents must be relative to the repository root. Absolute filesystem paths are prohibited. External resources must be referenced via their remote URL.

Sources: CO-4, SF-5.

## S-3 — Test Coverage Floor

Every new or modified Python module must maintain >= 80% test coverage. New modules must have > 0% coverage before merge. Verify with:
```
python -m pytest tests/ --cov=devolaflow --cov-report=term-missing
```

Source: CP-2.

## S-4 — No Ghost Features

Every feature listed in CHANGELOG.md must have corresponding working code, tests, and (if applicable) documentation. Do not add CHANGELOG entries for code that does not yet exist.

Source: CP-1.

## S-5 — No Silent Failures

Never suppress errors with try-catch (or equivalents) without logging, re-throwing, or returning explicit error states. Only ignore errors if explicitly requested for non-critical "best-effort" execution.

## S-6 — Protected Branch Workflow

NEVER push directly to protected branches (main, master, yc_dev, production). Always create a new feature branch, commit changes there, and propose a Merge Request or Pull Request.

## S-7 — External Resource URLs

External tools and benchmarks MUST be referenced by their remote GitHub URL. Local clone paths MUST NOT be hardcoded in any agent-facing file.

Sources: SF-6, SI-7.

# Architecture Rules (P1) — Core Architectural Decisions

## A-1 — 4-Layer Agent Hierarchy (P1–P5)

### P1 Dispatcher-Not-Implementer
Dispatcher agents (Project, Stage, Wave) MUST NOT perform work directly. Only Task Agents execute actual work. Tool enforcement: L0-L2 MAY use Read, Glob, Grep, SemanticSearch for planning/orchestration. L0-L2 MUST NOT use Write, StrReplace, Shell, or EditNotebook to implement — delegate to L3 Task Agents via the `Task` tool. Trivial exception: single file, < 20 lines — P1 waived.

### P2 Minimal Context
Each agent layer receives only the context it needs:
- L0 Project Agent: ~3K tokens (workflow template + status)
- L1 Stage Agent: ~5K tokens (stage def + predecessor summaries)
- L2 Wave Agent: ~4K tokens (task list + dependency map)
- L3 Task Agent: ~8K tokens (task spec + owned files + rules)

### P3 Structured Messages
All inter-layer communication uses typed YAML message schemas (TaskDispatch, StatusReport, ExceptionEscalation). Free-form natural language between layers is prohibited.

### P4 Bounded Retry
Every loop has a max_iterations ceiling. Every failure triggers a classified response (retry / escalate / abort). No infinite loops. Escalation always moves upward: Task→Wave→Stage→Project→Human.

### P5 Artifacts as Contracts
Layers communicate through artifact files, not shared memory or conversation history. Each artifact has a defined schema. The producing layer writes; the consuming layer reads. No bidirectional shared state.

## A-2 — P6 Preserve Cached Prefix

Dispatch payloads MUST honour the canonical layout declared in `schemas/lean-dispatch.yaml#layout_invariant`. Use `devolaflow.compressor.assert_dispatch_layout(payload)` before send. New top-level keys MUST be appended after `gate` (position 12). Reordering existing keys is a release blocker.

## A-3 — Context Token Budgets

Context profiles (`workflow-system/agent/context_profiles.yaml`) must define explicit token budgets per task type. Budgets are enforced by priority-based allocation: critical sections first, then important, then supplementary.

| Layer | Budget | Role |
|-------|--------|------|
| L0 Project | ~3K tokens | Workflow template + status |
| L1 Stage | ~5K tokens | Stage def + predecessor summaries |
| L2 Wave | ~4K tokens | Task list + dependency map |
| L3 Task | ~8K tokens | Task spec + owned files + rules |

Source: CO-3, SI-6.

# Conventions Rules (P2) — Coding & Format Standards

## C-1 — Pre-Commit Verification Checklist

Before committing to this repository, verify:
1. `python -m pytest tests/ -q` — all tests pass
2. `ruff check src/ tests/` — no lint errors
3. `ruff format --check src/ tests/` — formatting correct
4. No absolute filesystem paths introduced in agent-facing files
5. CHANGELOG updated if user-visible changes were made

Source: CP-7.

## C-2 — Lean Message Format

Inter-layer messages (TaskDispatch, StatusReport) must use the lean format defined in `schemas/lean-dispatch.yaml` and `schemas/lean-report.yaml`. Verbose prose descriptions are prohibited in dispatch/report YAML. Use verbatim compaction (key_facts lists, cause→effect notation) instead of summarization.

Source: CO-1.

## C-3 — Verbatim Extraction

`key_facts` in predecessor artifacts and `delta` in status reports must be verbatim extractions from source. Never paraphrase file paths, error messages, metric values, or commit hashes. This prevents hallucination risk per the LLM Scaling Paradox research.

Source: CO-2.

## C-4 — Tiered Line Budget

Agent-facing skill files are subject to tiered line-count ceilings:

| Tier | Ceiling | Files |
|------|---------|-------|
| Default | < 500 | `workflow-system/agent/SKILL.md` |
| Large | ≤ 1000 | `workflow-system/agent/references/*.md` (8 files) |
| XL | ≤ 1600 | `workflow-system/agent/examples/*.md` (3 files) |

Verify with:
```bash
wc -l workflow-system/agent/SKILL.md workflow-system/agent/references/*.md workflow-system/agent/examples/*.md
python -m pytest tests/test_integration.py::test_skill_md_under_500_lines tests/test_reference_size_budgets.py -v
```

Source: SF-1.

## C-5 — Required Frontmatter Keys

SKILL.md frontmatter (YAML between `---` delimiters) must include ALL of: `id`, `version`, `purpose`, `triggers`, `tier`, `token_estimate`, `last_updated`, `name`, `description`. The `description` field must describe WHEN/WHY to activate the skill (trigger conditions), not WHAT the skill does.

Source: SF-2.

## C-6 — Version Consistency

The version string must match `src/devolaflow/__init__.py` `__version__` in ALL canonical 7 locations:

1. `workflow-system/agent/SKILL.md` — frontmatter `version:`, banner, body "Current version:" text
2. `workflow-system/agent/workflow-skill.yaml` — identity section
3. `pyproject.toml` — version field
4. `scripts/generate_human_docs.py` — `SOURCE_VERSION`
5. `tests/test_smoke.py` — version assertion
6. `README.md` — badge and version example
7. `workflow-system/human/demo/benchmark-results/index.html` — `SAMPLE_DATA` version

Source: SF-3.

## C-7 — Valid Reference Links

Every `references/xxx.md` path mentioned in SKILL.md must correspond to an actual file under `workflow-system/agent/references/`. Valid references: `agent-hierarchy.md`, `context-isolation.md`, `decomposition-gate.md`, `execution-protocol.md`, `message-schemas.md`, `meta-framework.md`, `repo-modes.md`, `team-roles.md`.

Source: SF-4.

## C-8 — Always Use Braces for If

Always use braces for if, else if, and else branches in C++. No single-line unbracketed bodies allowed.

# Workflow Rules (P3) — Development Process

## W-1 — Iteration Planning Gate (SI-1)

Before starting any version iteration, produce a research/analysis artifact identifying gaps between current state and target goals. No implementation without documented gap analysis. Analysis artifacts live in `.local/research/`. The gap analysis must enumerate: (a) specific deficiencies found, (b) priority ranking, (c) proposed fixes with file-level scope. This gate is the entry point for SI-2 through SI-10.

## W-2 — NineS-Driven Analysis (SI-2)

For external reference analysis, run NineS deep analysis:
```
nines -f json analyze --target-path <path> --depth deep --agent-impact --keypoints
```
For end-of-iteration self-evaluation, run NineS self-eval with the repo's canonical config:
```
nines -f json -c nines.toml self-eval --baseline-version <version> --golden-dir data/golden_test_set --samples-dir data/golden_test_set --src-dir src/devolaflow --test-dir tests --project-root .
```
Store raw JSON output in `.local/research/`. When NineS is unavailable, manual analysis following the same dimensions is acceptable but must be noted as manual.

## W-3 — Evaluation Before Release (SI-3)

Every pre-release requires an evaluation report covering: Code quality (0.20), Architecture rationality (0.20), Test adequacy (0.20), Maintainability (0.15), Compatibility (0.10), Performance impact (0.15). Version readiness threshold: weighted composite ≥ 8.5/10.

## W-4 — Benchmark Regression Guard (SI-4)

Any change to `task_adaptive_selector.py`, `context_profiles.yaml`, lean message schemas, SKILL.md sections, or gate modules requires EvoBench verification:
```
python -m pytest tests/test_benchmarks.py -v
```
Regression threshold: composite score must not drop >5% below baseline per scenario.

## W-5 — Skill Format Coupling (SI-5)

Changes to SKILL.md or CLAUDE.md trigger ALL of: (1) line count check ≤ 500, (2) `build-skill` for all 4 adapters, (3) benchmark run passes, (4) version consistency passes. Partial compliance is treated as full violation.

## W-6 — Context Budget Enforcement (SI-6)

Changes to `context_profiles.yaml` require running `python -m devolaflow.task_adaptive_selector <task_type> --verbose` for all affected task types and verifying no section marked `critical` was dropped.

## W-7 — Iteration Retrospective (SI-8)

After completing a version release, produce a retrospective artifact summarizing: (1) Gaps identified, (2) What was implemented, (3) What was deferred and why, (4) Key learnings. Store in `.local/research/`.

## W-8 — Convergence Round Reinforcement (SI-9)

Multi-round convergence iterations MUST use the reinforcement mechanism (`src/devolaflow/gate/reinforcement.py`). Maximum 5 reinforcement rules per round, severity-filtered. If score stagnates for 2+ rounds → escalate to human.

## W-9 — Test-Then-Commit Protocol (SI-10)

Every iteration follows this strict pre-commit sequence — all 6 must pass:
1. `python -m pytest tests/ -q` — all tests pass
2. `ruff check src/ tests/` — no lint errors
3. `ruff format --check src/ tests/` — formatting correct
4. `python -m pytest tests/test_version.py -v` — version consistency
5. `python -m pytest tests/test_benchmarks.py -v` — no benchmark regressions
6. `make check-cursor-skill` — exit 0

## W-10 — Version Bump Protocol (CP-3)

When bumping the version, update ALL tracked locations consistently using `scripts/bump_version.py`. After bumping, run `python -m pytest tests/test_version.py -v` to verify.

## W-11 — Gate Module Changes (CP-4)

Changes to `src/devolaflow/gate/` require running the full gate test suite:
```
python -m pytest tests/test_gate.py -v
```

## W-12 — SKILL Changes Require Adapter Build (CP-5)

Changes to SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, or workflow-skill.yaml require running `build-skill` and verifying all 4 adapter outputs build successfully and stay within their budgets.

## W-13 — Context Optimization Benchmarks (CP-6)

Changes to `task_adaptive_selector.py`, `context_profiles.yaml`, or lean message schemas require running:
```
python -m pytest tests/test_benchmarks.py -v
```

## W-14 — Benchmark Verification (CO-5)

Context optimization changes must demonstrate improvement (or no regression) via EvoBench benchmarks. Baseline metrics are stored in `benchmarks/devolaflow_context/baselines/`.

## W-15 — Section Relevance (CO-6)

Context profiles must ensure task-type-relevant sections are marked `critical`, while unrelated sections are `skip`. Verify by running `task_adaptive_selector.py <task_type> --verbose` and inspecting skipped sections.
